reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be found in deep water around rock, wood, or hard bottom areas. Crappie and sand bass will be in the middle of the lake eating small shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Find offshore bass with a livescope and use umbrella rigs. Shallow bass can be caught with a weightless 5 inch stick bait in shad and bluegill patterns around docks. Crappie are congregated on main lake brush piles biting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing will be tough until the next warming trend. Based on past cold snaps, expect the Arctic blast to push bass more firmly into true winter patterns.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass will be biting at the hot water discharge, or schooled up on deep main lake humps and drop-offs biting Carolina rigs, Alabama rigs and jigging spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Target white bass and hybrid striped bass with 5/8 ounce or 3/4 ounce white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with stinger hook. Slow-smoking upwards off the bottom with these same slabs will produce when fish are more turned on. Largemouth bass are readily caught with these same tactics near timber.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie enter a hibernation state when the water drops into the 40s, so expect the bite to be slow. Crappie will be deep, then suspend higher in the water column on bright and sunny days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Due to inclement weather and dropping water temperature the bass bite is slow. Crappie enter a hibernation state when the water drops into the 40s, so expect the bite to be slow. Crappie will be deep, then suspend higher in the water column on bright and sunny days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 62 degrees; Redfish have been slow, with a few 5-10 pound fish coming from 5-10 feet of water on rattle traps, gold and silver spoons, and shrimp from the bank, and following the winter storm this past weekend the colder conditions have further slowed the overall bite, with catfish, stripers, and black bass all remaining sluggish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on docks 15-30 feet deep. Roaming crappie are suspended in the top third of the water column in 30-40 feet. Largemouth bass are decent using jigs, Alabama rigs, and swimbaits on main lake points, creek channels, or on banks in the late afternoons with crankbaits and chatterbaits on main lake rock and docks. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs and flukes. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 10.20 pounds are good stroking a creature bait, in Lone Star Disco color, on the ledges in 15-18 feet of water. Shallow bass can be caught with crankbaits on the rocks and docks and Alabama rigs around main lake pockets and points suspended. Crappie are fair to 12 inches on minnows and white and chartreuse or shad colored jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: After the ice storm expect the largemouth bass bite to start off slow, improving as the sun warms the water. If the bass are finicky, downsize to a shaky head or a Ned rig and just let it soak.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: When this happens a rattle trap, chatterbait, Alabama rig, or suspended jerkbait will work for the bass as they start schooling up again and feeding. Morning temperatures are around 15 degrees with snow and ice, so the bass will be very lethargic.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass, and stripers are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair when a light weight or weightless soft plastic is worked slowly along rocky points and grass edges near deep water. Expect the largemouth bass to slow due to the freeze, but the striped bass should fire in the next couple of weeks.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, bass, and white bass are being caught from the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast on numbers of largemouth bass and limits of eater sized channel catfish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass action is good, especially on jerkbaits, while catfish may move into the schools but are more often holding below them; focus on deeper water with soft bottoms where shad tend to concentrate. Crappie have been productive in 15-24 feet around structure, with minnows and hair jigs outperforming plastics lately, though many bites have been very light. Hybrid stripers are responding well to dead-sticking in 22-38 feet, with others catching fish on slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad; expect to sort through some juvenile hybrids mixed in with white bass, so check identification resources if needed.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie enter a hibernation state when the water drops into the 40s, so expect the bite to be slow. Crappie will be deep, then suspend higher in the water column on bright and sunny days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie enter a hibernation state when the water drops into the 40s, so expect the bite to be slow. Crappie will be deep, then suspend higher in the water column on bright and sunny days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: The freeze should push bass to deeper water. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass should push off the banks to the first drop-offs in 10-25 feet of water. Bass may be in the deeper water near the dam, the rocks near the dam will be difficult with the forecasted north wind. Bass will be lethargic due to the cooler water temperature so fish slowly with soft plastics or deep diving crankbaits. Expect a slow bass bite.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures are 37-40 degrees, and bass are very slow due to weather conditions. Lake Fork crappie fishing is in a full winter pattern and fishing is great. You can still find some crappie on brush piles in 18-25 feet. There are some crappie on bridges and tire reefs. Crappie are also on some main lake points and ledges in 18-32 feet relating to the bottom or small stumps. Lots of patterns are working for catching loads of crappie this winter.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 12-20 feet of water on structure with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Expect largemouth bass to be below the thermocline and tight to structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14-16 feet on brush on jigs. Bass are slow with slow moving baits like Carolina rig or crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small jigs worked on structure from Bentwater to the river near Tin Top. Largemouth bass are best on warmer days near deeper docks and deeper structure working soft plastics very slowly. Some largemouth are on the channel ledges where the bait fish are holding.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair at night in the river may. Expect the black bass and white bass to be slow.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass action is still very good in the back lakes off both forks where anglers can find slightly cleaner water, and on the south end bass are holding in secondary drop-offs and have moved deeper for cover and more stable temperatures; productive baits include deep-diving crankbaits. Crappie are tight to structure in 10-14 feet and are being caught on live minnows and hand-tied jigs, with dark colors working best in the stained water and presentations kept close to cover.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Based on past cold snaps, expect the Arctic blast to push bass more firmly into true winter patterns.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in deep water with crankbaits, rattle traps or chatterbait.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be found in deep water around rock, wood, or hard bottom areas. Crappie and sand bass will be in the middle of the lake eating small shad.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: After the ice storm and consistently below-freezing temperatures this week, crappie are expected to push into deeper water and settle into a true winter pattern near the dam. Crappie are holding tight to timber in deeper water off of the channels. Bigger crappie are moving off onto the flats to feed early morning then returning to the timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been limited due to inclement weather, but crappie should bunch up in deeper water. Before the front the crappie were good in 25-30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Any rock around the lake has been able to produce some bass bites on shad imitating baits. Also, there are schools of bass chasing around balls of shad.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush, roaming, and on the power line pylons biting minnows. White bass, catfish and crappie are roaming fish in 18-24 feet of water. Largemouth bass have started feeding on crawfish, so red and crawfish pattern baits will be a key to catching bass. Largemouth bass are in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks with red chatterbaits, red rattletraps, and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Predominant species in the fishery include plentiful white bass, strong channel and blue catfish, largemouth bass, striped bass, crappie and sunfish, giving anglers multiple targets depending on how you are fishing. White bass may still school and react to fast lures, bass will relate to deeper cover, and catfish can be found along main lake channels with cut bait or shad offerings.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been limited due to inclement weather, but crappie should bunch up in deeper water. Crappie are fair in 30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: After several days with freezing temperatures focus on large schools of bait fish to catch bass with Alabama rigs, jerkbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow on medium diving crankbaits on main lake rocky points. Crappie are good on white or chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on suspending jerkbaits and large swimbaits on grass lines. Crappie are slow with white or chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie numbers remain strong, while catfish action has been slow. Largemouth bass are excellent on suspending jerkbaits and large swimbaits on grass lines. Crappie are slow with white crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Expect bass to group up off the bottom under cover this weekend. With the full moon anticipate quality fish over quantity because the bigger bass should bite. Before the Arctic blast largemouth bass were good for catches up to 7 pounds. A 13 pound bass caught with a shaky head minnow. Target bass in 8-25 feet of water on river channel ledges, long tapering points close to deep water and outside Creek Bends. No crappie report.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will be slow but biting in deep water. Bass, hybrids and sand bass will be slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with suspended jerkbaits or Carolina rigs. Crappie are slow on white or chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish in those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair in deeper water along flats and levees.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in the creeks, and in 25-40 feet of water on brush and rocks. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass that are shallow will be around rocks and other hard cover. The suspended deeper black bass can be located with Livescope.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Target white bass and hybrid striped bass with 5/8 ounce or 3/4 ounce white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with stinger hook. Slow-smoking upwards off the bottom with these same slabs will produce when fish are more turned on. Largemouth bass are readily caught with these same tactics near timber. Based on past cold snaps, expect the Arctic blast to push bass more firmly into true winter patterns.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The crappie are still fair on bridge columns and deep timber with jigs in 20-28 feet. The largemouth bass bite has slowed down with the cold shallow water temperature.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth and smallmouth bass are holding tight to structure and docks in 8-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Based on past cold snaps, expect the Arctic blast to push bass more firmly into true winter patterns.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on live minnows and jigs on brush.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Expect the bite to improve for crappie and bass in February.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: The recent cold front will slow bass down and push them deeper.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good at the crappie house with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow in deep water with soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacking up in brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are slow on the main lake, but can be caught in creeks and rivers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving up the main channels migrating to their spring spawn points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Most bass are being caught on points and ledges near deep water, with slower-moving soft plastics and small minnow-style presentations producing best. While a 10 pounder was reported this week, the majority of bass being landed are in the 1-3 pound range. Crappie fishing has slowed as fish settle into a winter feeding pattern. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass will bite Alabama rigs and jerkbaits, small swimbaits, and jigging spoons. Crappie are good on brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Target offshore bass with livescope, and use umbrella rigs. Shallow bass can be caught with a weightless 5 inch stick bait in shad and bluegill patterns around docks. Crappie are congregated on main lake brush piles biting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early in the morning along deep grass edges. Bass are being caught on dropshot rigged finesse worms, light Texas-rigged soft stick worms, and crankbaits in 10–20 feet of water. Unseasonably warm winter conditions have kept bass from fully settling into typical winter patterns, but with a strong cold front expected, anglers should look for fish to shift toward the deeper, outer edges of grasslines. Dropshot rigs should continue to produce, and groups of bass may begin relating more closely to schools of shad in the main river channel.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Expect the cold front to stack bass near the discharge biting any shad related lure. Bass will be near deeper humps and drop-offs biting Carolina rigs, Alabama rig and jigging spoons. Bass will be offshore until water is back in the 60s.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: White bass and hybrid striped bass can be caught with white 5/8 ounce and 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs as the water is now too cold for faster tactics. When active fish are found, these slabs can be reeled up off bottom slowly while observing 2D sonar or Garmin LiveScope for follows. Many largemouth bass are being caught with a white 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab in 25-35 feet near timber and around isolated patches or pieces of cover.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is very slow. Finding crappie is not an issue, but the bite is very hit-or-miss.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be offshore biting Carolina rigs, jerkbaits or small swimbaits. Crappie will be scattered.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are finding success using rattle traps, gold and silver spoons, and some H&H plastics, with a few redfish also being caught from the bank/ Catfish action has been slow, and both stripers and black bass remain sluggish overall as conditions stay tough across the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Then crappie, bass, and hybrids will push deeper. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Crappie are good on docks in 10-15 feet, 20-30 feet on offshore brush piles, with roamers suspended top third of the water column in 30-40 feet. Largemouth bass are fair using medium crankbaits, Alabama rigs, and swimbaits for deeper schooling fish. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.34 pounds are good on shallow crankbaits on the rocks and docks and Alabama rigs around main lake pockets and points suspended. Crappie are good to 12 inches on minnows, or white and chartreuse or shad colored jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles in 11 feet and shooting jigs under docks in 18-22 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie should bunch up in deeper water. Crappie are fair in standing timber suspended 25-30 feet down with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Once the water temperatures fall below 44 degrees the bite will be tough on the lake, so target the river for the best success with bouncing a jigging spoon off the bottom for catfish, bass, white bass, yellow bass and drum. Before the cold front, rattletraps, jerkbaits, Alabama rigs, chatterbaits will all work and a fluke will work in the salvinia when the bass are jumping in it.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass activity remains slow overall, but some redfish and catfish are still being caught from the bank.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass have moved out a little bit deeper with the colder nights.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite continues to improve. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 14-22 feet of water around bridge pylons, brush piles, and docks. Guides report conditions improving, with larger crappie showing up more frequently.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are also picking up some black bass from the bank, along with white bass and a few crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass fishing has been slow, with most fish relating to timber in 6-10 feet of water, as well as off extended points.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek largemouth bass and channel catfish are extremely abundant.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been good along the edges and offshore, where fish are chasing shad schools. Crappie have been productive in 15-24 feet of water and near structure, with minnows, plastics, and hair jigs producing, though many bites have been very light. Hybrid striped bass are showing good numbers in 18-37 feet of slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad, with many keepers mixed in with juvenile hybrids and white bass.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Black bass are slow.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass should push off the bank due to the cold temperature. Before the cold front shallow bass could be with rattletraps over grass and in front of the reeds in the mornings, then with Carolina rigs and shaky heads in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is still slow, but picks up midday to evening. Black bass are moving up and down as the weather permits. Crappie are being caught in as shallow as 1 feet of water in the backs of creeks with a small clear clouser. Lake Fork crappie fishing is in a full winter pattern and fishing is great. You can still find some crappie on brush piles in 18-25 feet. There are some crappie on bridges and tire reefs. Crappie are also on some main lake points and ledges in 18-32 feet relating to the bottom or small stumps. Lots of patterns are working for catching loads of crappie this winter.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are related to wind-blown points and deeper rock ledges, with a few fish caught on crankbaits in 10–15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good inn 14-16 feet of water on brush with jigs and minnows. Bass are good on main lake points in 8-12 feet with crankbaits or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Best crappie action continues to be from Bentwater to above Hunter Park on small jigs and minnows. Look for suspended crappies on standing structure and under deeper docks. Black bass continue to be fair to good to 5 pounds on soft plastics around main lake points and near laydowns in the river above Granbury. Best action for black bass are on those warmer days and afternoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 7.5 pounds on jigs fished up river. Crappie are fair on jigs fished up river.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Move small slabs and small swimbaits on stinger hooks very slowly or even deadstick.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are on the move around grass in shallow sunny banks.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Lake Houston is in excellent condition and fishing has been on fire, with crappie and white bass being caught at a rapid pace and anglers consistently filling quality boxes. Crappie are producing well in the East Fork and Lucious Bayou on small hand-tied jigs, soft plastics, and live minnows, while white bass are actively feeding throughout the system, especially around Jesse H. Largemouth bass fishing remains solid, with healthier, larger fish being caught on deep drop-offs, under docks, along ledges, and secondary points using grubs, Texas-rigged worms, and crankbaits.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting well on jigs, dropshot rigged finesse worms, and crankbaits in 6–17 feet of water. With a strong cold front expected to move through, anglers should be on the lookout for bass shifting into more traditional winter patterns.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting jigs, Carolina rigs, and dropshot out deep, and some action on docks with a jig and dropshot.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass will bite Alabama rigs and jerkbaits, small swimbaits, and jigging spoons. Crappie and white bass are good in the main basin.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on the humps or in 25-30 feet of water on structures hugging the silt bottom. Find threadfin schools and the crappie will be nearby. Small swimbaits on 5/8 ounce jigheads, minnows, or slabs will work. Expect a bi-catch of crappie, catfish, and sometimes some largemouth bass. Black bass are on laydowns and rock piles in 15-20 feet. Any super sharp drop-offs in around 15 feet of water are producing bass with Carolina rigged jigs and 5/8 ounce jigs with a jerkbait soft plastic minnow attached. Free swim it over the bass if you have live scope.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie should bunch up in deeper water. Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Any rock around the lake has been able to produce some bass bites on shad imitating baits. Also, there are schools of bass chasing around balls of shad.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow to fair in 15-38 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Black bass fishing has been slower, with fish holding tight to structure and timber in deeper water and responding best to slower presentations. White bass and hybrid stripers are scattered but can be found schooling at times, while crappie remain near structure in deeper water, feeding lightly as winter patterns settle in.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Crappie should bunch up in deeper water. Crappie are fair in 30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on most of the lake fishing the hydrilla. Bass are spawning in the warmer waters but most are spawning in the 5-10 feet. Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 22-30 feet. Minnows and larger crappie jigs will catch some nice slabs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow on square bill crankbaits or Carolina rigs. Crappie are good on white or chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on deep Carolina rigs and deep crankbaits in 15-18 feet of water. Crappie are fair in the trees with white or chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations are strong, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth bass are slow on Alabama rigs or suspending jerkbaits. Crappie are fair with white crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-5 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding back in the shade around heavy cover to escape the sunlight. Early morning and late evening topwater is also effective for targeting bass. Baitfish are in the backs of pockets and upriver with the bass close behind. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Expect the crappie bite to shut off as fish scatter in deeper water. Crappie will be lethargic, but action should pick up in February.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass are fair to 5 pounds on a variety of shad patterned baits. No reports of crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in deep water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on small or large swimbaits. Crappie are slow on clear jugs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been steady in deep water around structure in 40-50 feet of water on live bait but can probably be targeted with deep water baits and deadsticking methods.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in about 21-23 feet. Bass moved to deep ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish in those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair and also moving out from brush and in the deeper water along flats and levees reports of catches on bridge pillars.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Back bass can still be caught around hard cover.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair. Crappie are fair at the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: White bass and hybrid striped bass can be caught with white 5/8 ounce and 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs as the water is now too cold for faster tactics. When active fish are found, these slabs can be reeled up off bottom slowly while observing 2D sonar or Garmin LiveScope for follows. Many largemouth bass are being caught with a white 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab in 25-35 feet near timber and around isolated patches or pieces of cover. Largemouth can still be found on warmer days on the outside edge of the thin band of hydrilla growing around the 15 feet mark, but many largemouth bass are being caught with the white 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab in 30-50 feet near timber, near…
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The crappie have been slow, but there is a steady bite at the 2 mile bridge on minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass bite improved after the big warm up on soft plastics on shallow ledges and ends of docks.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hanging on structure and stumps in 18-25 feet of water, be patient and have a variety of jig color and styles as it can vary day to day.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow, but with the right conditions you can have fun. Bass are fair on suspending jerkbaits, crankbaits, jigs, and shaky head finesse worms in 8–17 feet of water. Schools of bass are also roaming open water following shad and can be targeted with jerkbaits when they are active. With a strong cold front expected, anglers should look for bass to shift more toward deeper offshore structure such as rocky ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with fish scattered on brush piles and roaming in 20-30 feet of water with minnows. Bass are slow and scattered.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and lethargic with fish scattered in 15 feet of water. Crappie are very finicky, so use live bait and be ready to feel the light bite. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on the main lake brush 20-30 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 20 feet of water. Largemouth bass are slow using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass slow this week. Crappie are good under bridge pylons on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 20-25 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Bass are fair on spinnerbaits in 5-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to migrate shallow for the spawn. A lot of bass are hanging around the rocky areas feeding on crawdads and shad. Alabama rigs and jerk baits have produced larger bass. Crappie are good on brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be shallow and deep. If you like to livescope, offshore bass can be targeted with an umbrella rig, and a minnow on a jig head. Shallow bass can be caught with a weightless 5 inch stick bait in shad and bluegill patterns around docks. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with the best bite in the afternoon. Bass are fair to good. Unusually warm winter temperatures have many bass positioning in pre-spawn staging areas. Anglers may need to sort through smaller fish at times, but staying patient can still produce quality bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite slow, but a few can be caught on spinnerbaits slow rolled around timber 3-7 feet. Finding crappie is not an issue, but the bite is very hit-or-miss.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow with soft plastics. Crappie are slow on structures, and roaming in openwater.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Channel catfish are also slow, and black bass fishing continues to be sluggish across the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Crappie are good on docks in 10-15 feet, 20-30 feet on offshore brush piles, with roamers suspended top third of the water column in 30-40 feet. Largemouth bass are fair using medium crankbaits, Alabama rigs, and swimbaits for deeper schooling fish. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5.34 pounds are good on the rocks with all-around jigs and shallow crankbaits, or docks with Alabama rigs around main lake pockets and points suspended over 18 feet. Crappie are excellent to 15 inches on main lake scattered brush piles in 11 feet and shooting jigs under docks in 18-22 feet with minnows, .and white/chartreuse or shad jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in standing timber suspended 25-30 feet down with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good piling up in areas with rock and trees near drops. Bass seem to be in shallower areas as the water temperature is not far below 60 degrees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with Alabama rigs, shad color rattle traps, spinnerbaits, suspended jerkbaits and underspins. The crappie were good but slowed after the warm weather.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Stripers and black bass fishing remains slow overall.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth bass fishing is picking up.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing has been excellent, with channel and blue catfish being caught from the shore, along with some black bass, crappie, and white bass also taken by bank anglers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been fair, with fish holding in 5-10 feet of water around timber and brush piles, and soft plastics continuing to produce the best results.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to produce numbers of tilapia, channel catfish and largemouth bass. Largemouth bass are good on a variety of baits worked near points on many areas of the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been active both nearshore and off shore, chasing shad schools. Brad personally caught one in 37 feet of water on a slab while fishing for hybrids. Crappie have been productive in 17-25 feet on and near structure, with minnows giving the best results, though plastics and hair jigs are also working; bites can be light, but some areas are producing good numbers. Hybrid striped bass are being caught in good numbers in 24-35 feet using slabs, spoons, large minnows, or shad, with both keepers and juvenile fish schooling alongside some white bass.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are reported to be fair to good with jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent roaming open water midlake to the dam with minnows or jigs. Black crappie are in 20-50 fish schools. White crappie are suspended individually in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with creature baits on cloudy days. Reports of 3-5 pound bass and limits of smaller bass. No report on crappie.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with rattletraps over grass and in front of the reeds in the mornings.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is slow but improves midday and evening. Lake Fork crappie fishing is nothing short of on fire right now. Any crappie bait you want to try should work right now.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are related to wind-blown points, though they are more scattered this week and actively feeding on shad. White bass and crappie action has slowed near Overlook.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with minnows on rock piles in 16-18 feet. Bass are good with jigs or crankbaits on main lake points in 12-16 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: There is good action on small grubs and slabs worked in shallow water to 10 feet. Largemouth bass are fair to good on soft plastics worked near major creek entrances and working laydowns in the back of creeks and in the river. Crappie action continues to be good to excellent working submerged structure from Bentwater north.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Fishing has been excellent across the system, with largemouth bass on fire and being caught on drop-offs, back lakes, river bends, and around cypress nubs in 4-6 feet of water using grubs, worms rigged on 3/16 or ⅛ ounce weights, RoboWorms, and crankbaits worked along ledges. Crappie fishing has been great in East Fork and Luce’s Bayou, where anglers are finding success tight to structure with small plastics, jigs, or minnows, and a spot-lock trolling motor is helpful in windy conditions.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are stacking up in predictable pre-spawn staging areas and are being caught on dropshot rigged finesse worms, crankbaits, and jigs in 8–12 feet of water. Bass are good on docks, grass, laydowns and in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow, but the mid morning through afternoon has been fairly good. Look for large balls of bait and look for suspended bass just below. Crappie and white bass are good in the main basin.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Unseasonably warm temperatures paired with gusty winds have left crappie scattered and not holding to a predictable pattern. As colder temperatures return in the coming week, expect crappie to tighten back up on timber and structure along the creek channels. Bass anglers found a good bite in 4-6 feet of water along the creek channels this week.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on the humps or in 25-30 feet of water on structures hugging the silt bottom. Find threadfin schools and the crappie will be nearby. Small swimbaits on 5/8 ounce jig heads, minnows, or slabs will work. Expect a bi-catch of crappie, catfish, and sometimes some largemouth bass. Black bass are on laydowns and rock piles in 15-20 feet. Any super sharp drop-offs in around 15 feet of water are producing bass with Carolina rigged jigs and 5/8 ounce jigs with a jerkbait soft plastic minnow attached. Free swim it over the bass if you have live scope.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-35 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Some crappie are as deep as 24 feet with most in 10-15 feet of water. Crappie are on brush, roaming, and on the power line pylons biting minnows. Crappie eggs are still not fully developed yet. White bass, catfish and crappie are roaming fish in 18-24 feet of water. Largemouth bass have started feeding on crawfish, so red and crawfish pattern baits will be a key to catching bass. Largemouth bass are in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks with red chatterbaits, red rattletraps, and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair and being caught on plastics, spinners, and crankbaits around standing timber and creek structures, while striped bass are producing on spoons and live shad near deeper structures like the bridge area. Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs around docks and cover, white bass are fair on spoons and Alabama rigs, and catfish are fair to good on live bait throughout the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains good. Crappie are good with schools beginning to bunch up in standing timber and brush piles in 20-30 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 4 pounds with some better fish to 8 pounds being caught. Crappie no report.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass in the 8 feet water off of points and near channels. White crappie are good in 16-22 feet of water on brush and timber. Black crappie do not seem to be moving towards the shallows yet. Crappie are good on timber in 16-25 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Largemouth bass are good in the creeks with moving baits, or on docks with jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows. Sant bass and hybrids are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair and moving out from brush in the deeper water along flats and levees.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 35-50 feet on brush or timber using minnows or small natural colored jigs. Fish are biting 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can be caught shallow on square bill crankbaits and chatterbaits. Bass will be around hard cover and there feeding up for the winter colder temperatures. You will have to cover water, but it is a way to get some really big bass in the boat.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on the 2 mile bridge in 15-25 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Largemouth bass are tough. If the weather stays warm a few more weeks the fishing for the largemouth will improve.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have moved out off secondary ledges and humps on structure and stumps in 18-25 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Recent rains have dropped water temperatures back into the high 50s to low 60s, and while bass fishing has been on fire, the bite is expected to slow as cooler, wetter weather moves in with rain forecasted five out of the next seven days and highs in the 50s, bringing conditions back to normal for this time of year.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in deeper water mostly on trees and ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow at the crappie house with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow around docks with soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good from the bank with crankbaits midday. Crappie are good on docks and bridge columns using live minnows. Sand bass are good around schools of shad bouncing slabs and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-35 feet with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been somewhat challenging as fish are scattered throughout the water column, though most success is coming from shallow areas with available cover such as rocks or grass with some fish also being caught deep in 25-plus feet near adjacent 40-plus-feet of water. Crappie fishing is good around trees in 15-25 feet of water using 2-3 inch plastic minnows fished vertically, while catfish action remains steady in deep drains in 40-60 feet of water on prepared baits fished mostly vertical on small treble hooks. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles. A lot of bass are hanging around the rocky areas feeding on crawdads, shad and smaller fish. Alabama rigs and jerk baits have produced larger bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: If you like to livescope, offshore bass can be targeted with an umbrella rig, and a minnow on a jig head. Shallow bass can be caught with a weightless 5 inch stick bait in shad and bluegill patterns around docks. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been decent with the warmer weather. Deep grass edges are holding groups of bass. Bass are fair to good. Bass are not fully settled into a winter pattern due to unseasonably warm temperatures. Crappie are fair in 20-25 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on live minnows and small jigs next to timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Mornings bass bite is slow, but spinnerbaits and chatterbaits are fair in 3-5 feet of water on bushes or grass. Crappie are slow in the creek channels in 30-50 feet of water on timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass fishing remains slow, and black bass activity is also sluggish at this time.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on docks in 10-15 feet, 20-30 feet on offshore brush piles, with roamers suspended top third of the water column in 30-40 feet. Largemouth bass are fair using medium crankbaits, Alabama rigs, and swimbaits for deeper schooling fish. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs or trolling with deep crankbaits. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.5 pounds are good on all-around jigs and shallow crankbaits on the rocks and docks, or with 5-7 inch minnow style baits scoping main lake pockets suspended over 18-25 feet. Crappie are good to 1.75 pounds with minnows, and pink/yellow or shad jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles and shooting jigs under docks in 18-22 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: When the water temperature dips to the 40s bass will improve. The white bass and crappie are good running up and down the river systems. Crappie can be caught on jigs or minnows, and white bass are biting rooster tails. Bass are being caught on Alabama rigs, shad colored rattle traps, white chatterbaits, shad colored swimbaits, spinnerbaits and flukes. It was so warm last week bass could be caught with a topwater frog over the salvinia, so who knows what bass will hit as it warms up. Reports that a small wave of bass actually moved up on trees with the full moon and water temperatures at 57 degrees.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass action remains slow, and black bass activity is also sluggish overall.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The large and smallmouth bass fishing has also been decent. Bass can be caught on the outside edge of the hydrilla deadsticking a weighted wacky rig.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good stacks of white bass are being found on mid-lake points and drop-offs along sandy flats throughout the entire lake including the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch, and the spillway humps in 8-14 feet of water. Cast spinnerbaits and slabs, and watch for these flats as well as around deeper seawalls and shorelines. Hybrids can be caught with spinnerbaits or working a slab vertically with a fast up-and-down motion, strikes are immediate. A slow retrieve with a slab cast and reeled steadily back is also effective. Try rattle traps, spoons, umbrella rigs, slabs, or sassy shads to trigger bites. The crappie bite continues to improve. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 8–14 feet…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are finding good success catching blue and channel catfish from the bank, with some white bass, black bass, and crappie also being landed.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been fair, with most success coming from soft plastics worked around timber and along extended points.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast excellent fishing for eater-sized channel catfish and largemouth bass. Largemouth bass are good on a variety of baits worked near points on many areas of the lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been good across the lake, with strong numbers being caught offshore as fish chase shad schools, and many anglers finding success with jerkbaits and deep-diving crankbaits. Crappie have been productive in 17-25 feet of water, with minnows producing best, though plastics and hair jigs are also working, as fish are holding on structure in 13-24 feet and often biting lightly while still giving up good numbers. Hybrid stripers are being caught in good numbers in 19-35 feet of water on slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad, with some fish also coming on dead-sticking, though warmer temperatures have slowed that pattern; many juvenile hybrids are showing up, so anglers should…
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass are scattered and bigger bass are biting more in the evening in deeper water. No reports on crappie.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with rattletraps over grass, and in 4-10 feet of water with Carolina rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The warmer days are bringing some bass shallow as the water temperature ranges from 55-59 degrees. Lake Fork crappie fishing is nothing short of on fire right now. Any crappie bait you want to try should work right now.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are related to wind-blown points, actively feeding on shad. White bass and crappie action has been good, with solid numbers being caught near Overlook Park.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with jigs or minnows in 14-16 feet deep in brush piles and on rock piles. Bass are slow in about 12-14 feet near rock piles with slow moving baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Best fishing reports are for crappie from mid-lake to Hunter Park. Crappie are good on small jigs fished suspended near underwater structure and docks. Granbury sand bass action has been slow to fair on slabs and jigs fished on flats adjacent to the channels. Largemouth bass are good in numbers near major points in 15-30 feet of water and many are feeding with the sand bass and small striped bass. Some bigger largemouth are being taken on soft plastics near major creek entrances with some good reports coming from the river above Granbury.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on crankbaits fished up river around timber. Crappie are fair in deep water near the dam.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Deadsticking small slabs and small swimbaits on stinger hooks.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: In the main lake, largemouth bass are biting well around cypress knees and structure on grubs, deep-diving crankbaits, and spinnerbaits, holding on drop-offs edges during low pressure and moving deeper during high pressure. Catfish are being caught consistently around bulkheads and river channels near the train tracks on fresh-caught shad, while crappie fishing is outstanding in the East Fork and Luces Bayou in 8-12 feet of water tight to structure on minnows and small jigs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting well on dropshot rigged finesse worms, crankbaits, and finesse jigs in 8–17 feet of water. Large concentrations of panfish and gizzard shad are showing on sonar in the same areas where bass are being caught.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow, but can be caught along the bank with Texas rigged soft plastic worms, and some off of deeper brush on a Texas rigged baby brush hog. Had a few slow ups on topwater walking baits, but bass would not eat.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough due to the constant warm and cool trends. Most shad are in deep water while the bass seem to be setting up adjacent on summertime deep water spots. Crappie are in piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is excellent this week. Crappie have not fully transitioned to the winter pattern near the dam and lake bottom, but are still closely related to creek channels, timber, and brush. Crappie are biting well on jigs, live minnows, and a variety of presentations, with consistent action reported throughout the lake. Bass fishing was good this week.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-35 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have started feeding on crawfish, so red and crawfish pattern baits will be a key to catching bass. Largemouth bass are in 6 feet of water or less on docks, bulkheads and rocks with red chatterbaits, red rattletraps, and Texas rigs. White bass, catfish and crappie are roaming fish in 18-24 feet of water. Crappie are on brush, roaming, and on the power line pylons biting minnows. Crappie eggs are still not fully developed yet.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are biting best around timber and submerged structure in 3-8 feet of water using soft plastics, crankbaits, and Texas rigs, while catfish are fair in deeper holes and along the banks on cut bait, stink bait, and shad. Crappie are being caught around flooded timber in 4-7 feet of water on small jigs and minnows, and occasional white bass and hybrid stripers are being picked up on spoons and shad-style baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good to excellent in deep and shallow water. Crappie are good fishing brush piles and timber in 12-25 feet with large schools of shad in the area.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, and sand bass all have continued to flourish around many parts of the lake. Crappie have been slow this week again.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 6 pounds with a few fish up to 8 pounds. Bass are in 10-25 feet on umbrella rigs, swimbaits, crankbaits and jerkbaits. Slabs and spoons are also working in the schools. Crappie no report.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow, but can be caught in deep water on minnows. Crappie are feeding on shad in the creek. Hybrids are biting top waters or slabs. Black bass and sand bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been slow to fair. Crappie are fair to good under docks. Largemouth bass are good using a slow approach in the cold water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair moving out from brush to deeper water along flats and levees.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Fish are biting 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair in 35-50 feet on brush or timber using minnows or small natural colored jigs. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can still be caught shallow on hard structure such as rock or stumps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good with catches on the concrete structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, focus on roaming schools following baitfish in open water.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Flukes, slabs and small jigs are best in 28-50 feet. Crappie are good on the 2 mile bridge on small tandem rigged jigs in 22-28 feet. Largemouth bass have been slow the past few weeks.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remain active on structure in 15-20 feet with jigs being the main focus, day to day color and size preference can change so have the tackle box stocked with a variety of jig heads and plastics.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been good on warmer days in 3-8 feet of water using lipless crankbaits, jerkbaits, and chatterbaits, while cooler days require slowing down with wacky worms and light Texas rigs. Crappie fishing has been fair, with some good reports coming from the backs of creeks in 4-7 feet of water on Road Runners around flooded timber, though upcoming rain is expected to stain the water and may take a few days to clear.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has slowed, but if you slow your presentation down considerably you can still get some good bites. Bass are fair along rocky ledges with brush in 10–25 feet of water using football jigs and shaky head finesse worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie improved to good at the crappie house with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with slow moving baits off the bank. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs under bridge columns.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-30 feet on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in 20-30 feet of water on soft plastics. Crappie are good under trees in the coves with jigs and minnows. Cold weather has driven bass to quick drop areas from 15 to 45 feet of water. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught utilizing a slow approach in deep water with deep crankbait or jigs around ledges, or a Carolina rigged finesse worm.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow but Texas rigs can catch a few in 5-7 feet of water on timber. Offshore brush piles in 22-30 feet have both bass and crappie. Smaller jigs for bass like Mini Viper Jigs are good. Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed. Crappie are good in 20-60 feet of water on timber in the creek channels. The primary species being caught is black crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remain deep around main lake docks using minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
