reports.text: Black bass to 9 pounds are good on jigs around bait balls in open water, and squarebill crankbaits in 2-4 feet of water. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 13-18 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on rock piles in around 10-12 feet of water slowly working jigs or craw worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The water temperature fell so low the Florida bass will take their time coming out the funk they are in. There is a good current in the river so bass and white bass should be good in the cuts, turns and drops.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek largemouth bass action continues to be excellent on soft plastics and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been fair on minnows and jigs and are being fished pretty heavy. Largemouth bass have been good on shad schools and offshore structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with some big fish being caught in shallow water with chatterbaits and rattle traps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair suspending jerk baits, spinner baits, and square bill crankbaits around creek channels in 5-10 feet. Offshore bass bite is fair with Alabama rigs, spoons and dropshots in 17-22 feet. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been as up and down as the weather and wind. With surface temperatures in the low 40s some crappie seem to be in shock. Hold those baits super still just above crappie and they will either bite or swim off.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is excellent on soft plastics fished near docks and main lake points. Crappie action is good as well with the abundance of fish deeper especially on those colder days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Use white slabs on a stinger hook with a small jig head with a power gulp minnow tied two feet above.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are decent if you can find some clear water in the back lakes. Crappie are tight to structure in the East fork and Luces bayou eating small hand tied jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-25 feet of water with minnows. A few catfish have been caught while fishing for crappie. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on rock piles and brush piles on sunny days. Docks always come into play on this lake so if you find the right ones you can catch a mess of bass. Look for deeper docks but if you do not find any bass try the outside edges. There are some nice grass patches around the lake as well and lots of bass can be found around some of those.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on deep flats and in river channels in 42-64 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 4-38 feet of water on brush piles, bridge pilings, and submerged cover close to a drop off ledges with minnows and jig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Starting to see fully developed egg sacks in crappie and white bass. Crappie, white bass and catfish have been as deep as 20 feet. Crappie are in 10-18 feet on offshore brush with minnows, or tight lining straight down in standing timber. Largemouth bass can be caught from 2-18 feet this week on docks, timber, bulkheads, rocks with Texas rigs, jigs, chatterbaits, and spinnerbait. Numbers of bass are in 5-7 feet of water.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Catching a lot of white bass in 15-25 feet on the south end with Ducktracker slabs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow due to the colder weather and while the power plant runs one generator. Crappie are slow in 30-35 feet of water around fallen timber near the dam area using minnows and pintail jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been caught on artificial grubs and minnows in Sanford Yake Cove and Bugbee. Very few reports of crappie this week.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair in shallow grass or on hard spots in 10 feet of water. Crappie are excellent with 1/16 or ⅛ ounce jigs in standing timber in 15 feet of water.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: We still have some bass that are being seen in deeper water in larger groups. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are fair with small swimbaits and Alabama rigs. Crappie are excellent with white and chartreuse jigs suspended on timber in 15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are staging to move shallow for the spawn preferring minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 8 pounds on umbrella rigs, jigs, swimbaits and spoons. Crappie are fair in timber in 35 feet of water suspended down 15-25 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: The crappie spawn typically begins around the first week of February near a full moon, but is highly dependent on lake level and water temperature. Crappie are still being found in the normal winter habitat in about 13-23 feet of water by the Live Scope anglers.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to bite and schooling up.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on deep diving crankbaits and Carolina rigs in 12 feet of water. Crappie are slow with 1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 35-39 feet of water with �¾ ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above at least 16 inches apart. Crappie are fair on brush in 18-28 feet of water moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats with minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair with only a few reported catches being made with a slab and jig combination fished on the bottom in 25-30 feet of water off main lake points and Pelican Island. Hybrid striper action fair on live bait and slabs fished in the same areas as the white bass.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good throughout the lake on jigs and minnows. Some bass being caught near the crappie house. If it’s a warm rain it may trigger the bass to transition shallow to feed

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is slower with the colder temps. Bass fishing is slower with the falling water temps.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Due to the influx of freshwater the creeks are flowing and the crappie bite is slow. Bass bite has been slow, with a few fish coming on spinnerbaits and chatter baits in 4-7 feet of water, Texas and Carolina rigs on main lake points in 12-18 feet, and big crankbaits in 18-25 feet. The deeper bass are moving with shad from day to day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on crankbaits and trick worms. Crappie are slow on minnows in 30 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: On colder winter days, shift to deeper water and slow down your presentations to attract sluggish bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-30 feet on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in 20-30 feet of water on soft plastics. Crappie are good under trees in the coves with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are hitting crankbaits and moving baits in the morning. Bass are moving to offshore structures 10-15 feet in the middle of the day hitting soft plastics, with brush hogs worms working best.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow and can be caught in grass 8-15 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working grass on the north end with worms, spinnerbaits or rattle traps. There continues to be a good bass bite in the grass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Those whites and hybrids on bottom features are best targeted with a white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab in ⅝-3/4 ounce.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Water clarity is 1-2 feet in windblown coves and bass have been biting on small-profiled flat sided squarebills in craw colors, dark colored jigs, and dark colored finesse worms on a shaky head. Windy, sunny banks and retaining walls are good bets for black bass. On warm, sunny days, small shad pattern flies might produce bass around submerged vegetation.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very slow. A few bass can be caught reeling spinnerbaits very slow around bushes and trees in 6-10 feet. Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed. Crappie are good in 20-60 feet of water on timber in the creek channels. The primary species being caught is black crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can still be found in deeper water on the main lake, minnows fished very close to the bottom may get a fish or two. Largemouth bass have been slow, the earliest pre-spawn fish may be found in wind sheltered water, especially on warmer sunny days.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6.41 pounds are excellent on squarebill crankbaits in 2-4 feet of water and on jigs around bait balls in open water. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 10-15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to group off points and offshore structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in deep timber with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on rock piles in around 10-12 feet of water slowly working jigs or craw worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: As the water increases to the upper 50s bass will be getting ready to spawn.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to draw in those largemouth bass anglers due to the warmer water of this power plant lake. Largemouth bass are being caught in numbers on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good on brush from 12-25 feet on minnows and jigs. Bass have been good cranking rocks and shad schools as well as plastics under shad schools and offshore structures.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Water clarity is 1-2 feet in windblown coves and bass have been biting on small-profiled flat sided squarebills in craw colors, dark colored jigs, and dark colored finesse worms on a shaky head.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in brush piles and rocky points early in the morning when the sun comes and warms the water with a square bill crankbait. Bass are being caught on the south end of the lake with football head jigs and power worms. Very few reports of crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Prefrontal bass bite bass was good shallow along the bank with shaky heads. During the front the fish should have moved deeper and slowed, but bass should return shallow as the weather warms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very slow but the bite is fair on Alabama rigs over deeper water 20-25 feet around baitfish. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been up and down just like the weather the last few weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow. Crappie are good in brush in 15 -20 feet on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass are good to 12 pounds on flukes and bass assassins fished near the river channel from Indian Harbor to the Peninsula. Crappie action continues to be good in deep water near submerged structures. Good crappies are also being caught in the river near Tin Top on small jigs. Largemouth bass are being caught near major creek entrances and in deeper holes in the river above Granbury.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are in 40 feet of water 5-10 feet off the bottom with white slabs on a stinger hook and thumper on the boat.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are in those areas eating grubs with 1/8 ounce and 1/4 ounce jig heads crawl imitations seem to work the best around structure. The crappie bite is slowly coming back, but the crappie are finicky and seem to be deep, hanging tight to structure in Luces Bayou, and in the East Fork.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow on rattletraps and squarebills in shallow water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: If you can brave these cold snaps it is a good time to target big bass with forward facing sonar.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Water clarity is 1-2 feet in windblown coves and bass have been biting on small-profiled flat sided squarebills in craw colors, dark colored jigs, and dark colored finesse worms on a shaky head.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 20-30 feet of water on brush piles and deep submerged timber. Crappie are hugging the bottom so you have to let a ⅛ ounce hand tied jig touch the bottom and then slowly lift to entice a bite. Slabs and 3-4 inch flukes have been getting them. Black bass are in 1-5 feet on rocks or concrete, and in 5-10 feet of water shoreline structure. Texas rigs and bass jigs are pulling them out of 15-20 feet deep brush piles. The dam has trees and brush bluegill and crappie are mixed in. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the warmer water from the scrapper cut into Dry creek. Crappie are slow while fish are primarily scattered with a few found in deeper brush piles using minnows. Sand bass are good at the discharge using small slab spoons and little George’s.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been caught on artificial grubs and minnows in Sanford Yake Cove and Bugbee. Crappie are slow with no reports this week.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in 15-20 feet of water Carolina rigs, and deep diving crankbaits. Bass are in deep schools with fish ranging 2-4 pounds. Crappie are excellent with fish 15-16 inches roaming in standing timber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: We still have some bass that are being seen in deeper water in larger groups. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with many fish 2-6 pounds. Crappie are excellent with white and chartreuse jigs suspended on timber in 20 feet of water.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services Report by Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were fair on jigs or hand ties.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with 9 pound catches possible on rage swimmers on umbrella rigs, small shad patterns swimbaits and jerkbaits to 10 feet suspended over deep water. Some bass reported upriver on hags half ounce tsunami jigs green pumpkin with trailer. Crappie are fair on minnows around Elm Creek, mouth of bullhollow and Ranger Cove suspended over deep water trees. White bass good on mine like in 30-45 feet of water on slabs and jigging spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Now getting ready for the Spring crappie spawning season. Crappie are still being found in the normal winter habitat in about 13-23 feet of water by the Live Scope anglers.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good to excellent on small swimbaits suspended in 12-18 feet of water. Crappie are slow with 1/16 ounce white crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs. Bass slow but will bite when located. Bass biting from deep to shallow depths following shad movement. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 35-39 feet of water using 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above spread at least 16 inches apart. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 18-28 feet deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass can be caught on live bait and slabs on humps near creek channels in 35-55 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair with a few reported catches being made with a slab and jig combination fished on the bottom in 25-30 feet of water off main lake points and Pelican Island. Hybrid striper action is also fair on live bait and slabs off main lake points, Pelican Island and Windsock Point in 30 feet of water or deeper.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very lethargic and slow to bite. Crappie and white bass are moving up the creek channels.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnow over brush 8-16 feet of water. Black bass are slow moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Those whites and hybrids on bottom features are best targeted with a white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab in ⅝-3/4 ounce.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Presenting crappie jigs or small flukes and swimbaits is key suspended over deep water. Crappie are good on bridge pilings and deep timber in 30 feet of water. The largemouth bite has been very slow.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 18-25 feet of water near drop-offs and rocky points. Bass fishing can be caught with soft plastics off main lake points and creek points off the banks.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working cliffs and ledges slow with jigs and Texas-rigged plastics such as worms, craw worms and creature baits to get most bites. Largemouth bass can be caught on the lower end hydrilla and grass with underpins and Alabama rigs. Some bass are under docks ⅜ ounce pumpkin jig or wacky rigged senko.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: On colder winter days, target deeper water and slow your presentations to entice lethargic bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in 15-20 feet of water soft plastics. Crappie are good under trees in the coves with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in 8-15 feet of water in the grass with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on soft plastics in the cuts, or with frogs over grass. Crappie are fair with jigs in flooded timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught in deep water with deep crankbait or jigs around ledges, or a Carolina rigged finesse worm.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Those on bottom features are best targeted with a Bladed Hazy Eye Slab in 5/8 ounce or 3/4 ounce in white color.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are very slow and difficult to catch while cold fronts are rolling through. Few bass can be caught in timber on Viper XP jigs on or near drop-offs like ditches and creeks in 7-11 feet. Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed. Crappie are good in 20-60 feet of water on timber in the creek channels. The primary species being caught is black crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the weeds on plastic worms or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered but can be found around brush piles and the deep water in front of main lake docks. Largemouth bass are in the earliest stages of their pre-spawn.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 2.5 pounds are slow on jerkbaits and crankbaits in 2-12 feet. The bass are in a normal winter pattern. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 9-15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in deep timber with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: This will be where the black bass and some white bass should be hanging around.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good dragging along the grass or near hydrilla in 14-20 feet of water with an Alabama rig or underspin with your favorite plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite has been tough with reports of fish being scattered. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 7-15 feet under bridge pylons, hidden brush piles throughout the lake or under docks. Crappie fisherman have been moving spot to spot finding limits. Lots of crappies in the 7-9 inch range. Limits of crappie will happen but you may catch a lot of small ones getting to your limit.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The warm water from the power plant continues to lure in the largemouth bass anglers and catfish anglers from all over the state. Channel catfish limits are common on prepared baits and largemouth to 7 pounds are good on soft plastics fished near points and creek channels. Largemouth bass catches of 40-60 fish a day are possible.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good early and late on the edges but slow working baits in and under shad schools can really produce. Watch points for schooling bass of all kinds early and late in the day. Crappie have been fair but hit or miss depending on whether the spot has been drained already.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught near the surface. Crappie are in the tree stumps near the shore.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are staged at the end of points and creek channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is best on the main lake around humps and ledges in 15-25 feet with Alabama rigs. Mid range bass are fair, suspended on timber in 12-15 feet with jerkbaits and large spinnerbaits. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been up and down just like the weather the last few weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow. Crappie are good in brush 15 -20 feet on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Some really big sandbass catches to 2.5lbs are being reported on slabs and 3 inch soft plastics. Crappie action is good in town near submerged timber and some good catches continue to be caught in the river near Tin Top. Best crappie baits continue to be small jigs or small minnows. Largemouth bass fishing is better on those warmer days. Best largemouth catches have been reported near creek entrances and near laydowns on the upper ends and are best on soft plastics worked slowly.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair up the river on jigs and crank baits. Crappie are slow in the river, but some are being caught in the main lake open water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water with soft plastics, or in 10-12 feet on structure with crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in open water in 20-25 feet with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on rock piles and brush piles on sunny days. Docks always come into play on this lake so if you find the right ones you can catch a mess of bass. Look for deeper docks but if you do not find any bass try the outside edges. There are some nice grass patches around the lake as well and lots of bass can be found around some of those. Largemouth bass can be caught in 7-15 feet of water on the outer edge of grass with shad patterned Alabama rigs, or crawfish colored rattle trap or chatterbait, or dragging senkos or 6 inch trick worms on the outer…
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on deep flats and in river channels in 40-60 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 4-38 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on the warm water side from mid lake into dry creek. Bass are spawning in some areas. Crappie are fair with minnows and pintail jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been caught on artificial grubs and minnows in Sanford Yake Cove, North Canyon and off the docks. No reports of Crappie this week.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on hard spots in 16-20 feet of water with Carolina rigs, dropshots, and deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are excellent roaming in standing timber when utilizing forward facing sonar.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: There are still some large groups of bass in deeper water hovering just off the bottom. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are fair while the water is heavily stained. Crappie are fair on brush piles and standing timber with a ⅛ ounce white crappie jig on a split shot.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. It is also important to slow down your retrieve this time of year to trigger these lethargic winter largemouth. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in the brush with a few catches off the dock, but the numbers are down.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are improving with a couple of fish over 10 pounds being caught, and several 7-8 pound fish. Crappie are good with minnows in deep trees out in front of Ranger Cove, Elm Creek and Bull Hollow. White bass good spooning on silver slabs and cash Masters in 30-35 feet on flats next to 45-50 feet drop.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: We have received some reports of crappie being caught in 8-10 feet of water. Black bass can be caught with Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with jigs and minnows in creeks off Lake Palestine. White bass can be caught on white curly tails and small crappie jigs, or spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in deep water around brush piles on minnows. The lake is starting winter off full, so crappie season should be great in March.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass bite is good with 3-5 fish schools in deep water biting small swimbaits on ⅛ ounce jigheads. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.text: Bass are scattered so cast spinnerbaits and crankbaits looking for active schools of fish. Crappie and white bass are moving up the creek channels.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good throughout the lake on jigs and minnows. Bass are fair or typical for this time of year. Bass are not shallow just yet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Those on bottom features are best targeted with a Bladed Hazy Eye Slab in 5/8 ounce or 3/4 ounce in white color.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The crappie have been good on deeper structures including bridge columns and deeper timber. Largemouth have been slow this week.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are holding deep in 20-30 feet of water on humps and ledges with brush and structure. Bass fishing slowed with the water temps dropping but look for fish to move up in coves and near docks on sunny days.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow. Few bass can be caught on main lake points with Carolina rigs and big crankbaits in 12-18 feet. No crappie report.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great with fish chasing shad deep or feeding shallow. Largemouth bass can be caught on the lower end hydrilla and grass with underpins and Alabama rigs. Some bass are under docks ⅜ ounce pumpkin jig or wacky rigged senko.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hit-or-miss with the best bite in the morning at 9 a.m. in 17 feet of water on structure with jigs. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: On colder days, look for fish in slightly deeper water and slow down your presentations to account for lethargic bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the Crappie House on jigs and minnows. Bass and catfish are slow deep and around rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-20 feet on the north end of the lake. White bass fishing is fair on flukes and slabs. Largemouth bass fishing is good around the docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-40 feet on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in shallow water soft plastics. Crappie are good under trees in the coves with jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are hitting crankbaits and moving baits in the morning. Bass are moving to offshore structures 10-15 feet in the middle of the day hitting soft plastics, with brush hogs worms working best when the water temperature is in the mid 50s.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow and can be caught in grass 5-10 ft with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.text: Bass can be caught in deep water with deep crankbait or jig around ledges, or a Carolina rigged finesse worm.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: At that time, change to using a thumper instead of a splasher, and change baits to white Bladed Hazy Eye 3/4 ounce slabs.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to stage for the spawn and putting on some good weight. Windy, sunny banks and retaining walls are good bets for black bass. On warm, sunny days, small shad pattern flies might produce bass around submerged vegetation.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Overall the bass bite is slow. Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed. Crappie are good in 20-60 feet of water on timber in the creek channels. The primary species being caught is black crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be slow, try offshore brush piles or deep water in front of main lake docks. Check way up in the backs of coves for largemouth bass with swimbaits.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in a normal winter pattern with a slow bite. Black bass to 4.22 pounds can be caught on minnow style baits and crankbaits in 2-6 feet. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 9-15 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: The bass pattern is strange with a lot of fish suspended on bait. You can catch bass dragging or cranking, or casting little swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite has been tough with reports of fish being scattered. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 7-15 feet under bridge pylons, hidden brush piles throughout the lake or under docks. Crappie fisherman have been moving spot to spot finding limits. Lots of crappies in the 7-9 inch range. Limits of crappie will happen but you may catch a lot of small ones getting to your limit.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass catches to 7 pounds are abundant on crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth has been fair on jerkbaits and deep cranks on offshore ledges and plastics worked slowly through the brush. Crappie have been fair and some nice catches reported, but everyone is out there after them and it is a matter of finding a spot that has not already been drained prior to your arrival. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs jigging for them and getting ready for deadsticking when the water temperature drops a little more.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to stage for the spawn and putting on some good weight.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Look for birds working or schools of bait on the main lake and in mid-depths on chartreuse and white slabs or paddle tail swimbaits. Crappie are being caught on deeper structure cover using larger profile baits and also spider rigging open water, with the colder weather coming in docks will start producing again.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are staging at the end of points and creek channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow but can be caught targeting deeper edges of points fishing slowly with Carolina rigs, shaky heads, deep crankbaits. Hopefully this cold front will have bass staging in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 3-5 feet of water in timber or grass with chatterbaits, square bill crankbaits and flukes. The Lake Fork crappie fishing continues to be excellent as the surface temperatures continue to drop. If you find areas with tons of shad there will be crappie close by. Minnows are always a go to bait for crappie on Lake Fork. Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed. Crappie are good in the river channel timber.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting on minnows and jigs in about 15 feet of water near brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being caught on small jigs and minnows mid-lake near structure and in the river near Tin Top. Largemouth bass are still good near main lake points and in the river near laydowns on soft plastics worked slowly.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been very hungry lately even in the muddy water tight to structure in both the offshore structure and shallow structure. Crappie are good in deep water right to structure using small jigs to entice bites.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is tough with a few bites on jigs and soft plastics on brush and around docks. Suspended bass can be caught with a minnow style bait or jerkbait.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to stage for the spawn and putting on some good weight.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows in 12-16 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good on rock piles and brush piles on sunny days. Docks always come into play on this lake so if you find the right ones you can catch a mess of bass. Look for deeper docks but if you do not find any bass try the outside edges. There are some nice grass patches around the lake as well and lots of bass can be found around some of those.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, white bass and catfish have been as deep as 20 feet this week. Crappie are in 10-18 feet on offshore brush with minnows, or tight lining straight down in standing timber. Largemouth bass can be caught from 2-18 feet this week on docks, timber, bulkheads, rocks with Texas rigs, jigs, chatterbaits, and spinnerbait. Numbers of bass are in 5-7 feet of water.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Ducktracker slabs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with swim jigs, swimbaits, bladed jigs and Texas rigged worms on the inside and outside of hydrilla, or with dropshots around tilapia beds near scrapper cut. Crappie are slow on brush piles in 10-20 feet of water with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth are good with artificial grubs and minnows in Sanford Yake Cove, Bugbee and off the docks. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: We still have some bass that are being seen in deeper water in larger groups. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits, Carolina rigs and dropshots. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and standing timber with a 1/16 ounce white crappie jig on a split shot.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Seeing more 5-10 pound flathead catfish being caught on minnows in brush piles where crappie are usually.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with reports of a fish over 13 pounds caught and several to 6-7 pound fish on a variety of baits from deep diving crankbaits, jerk baits and umbrella rigs. Crappie fishing is good in the mouth of Elm Creek and also in Big Trees out in the Colorado River in front of Rangers Cove.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: We have received some reports of crappie being caught in 8-10 feet of water. The Black Bass and catfish bite has been slow. The anglers targeting Bass are using A-rigs.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good midlake to the southern on deep timber and channel ledges with jigs and minnows. No report for bass, but traditionally this lake fishes shallow for bass year round with jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Use live shad or small slabs and jigs. Bass are moving up with the lake level rising. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Anglers report that the bass fishery is slow. No reports of catfish or crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 30-38 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above working best spread at least 16 inches apart. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 18-28 feet deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats with minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass fishing can be rated fair with catches being made with a slab or jig combination fished on the bottom in 25-30 feet of water off main lake points and Pelican Island. Hybrid striper action is fair on live bait and slabs off main lake points, Pelican Island and Windsock Point in 30 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The white bass and largemouth bass are still putting on a show at Stillhouse with two angler catches over 100 fish in a morning. Then switch to a white, ⅝ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with spinner and stinger hook as the water cools and the fish slow down. There are plenty of largemouth bass and freshwater drum mixed in with the white bass in these same deep water areas. The shad-imitating 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab is the go to bait for these fish.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Slabs and swimbaits have been working best. The crappie are fair on jigs in 18-35 feet. Largemouth bass have been slow.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slow with the recent cold snap and falling water temps. Crappie fishing is tough.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great with fish chasing shad deep or feeding shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-20 feet on the north end of the lake. White bass fishing is slow but some are being caught up the river on flukes and slabs. Largemouth bass fishing is good around the docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair, look for birds working or schools of bait on the main lake and in mid-depths on chartreuse and white slabs or paddle tail swimbaits. Crappie are being caught on deeper structure and cover using larger profile baits and also spider rigging open water, with the colder weather coming in docks will start producing again.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service
